editorial:
Imagine being a dad who thinks he has everything under control, only to find out your teenage daughter is struggling with hard drugs. That is exactly where you meet Miles, a successful TV director who believes his strict rules are just for the best. When he sends his daughter Zoe to a rehab center in Utah, he expects her to be the only one fixing things. Instead, he is forced into a four-day workshop with a quirky leader named Gillian. You will feel the tension as Miles realizes that his need to control everything might actually be part of the problem. It is a heavy setup, but the movie keeps a grounded feel that makes you root for the family to heal.

The acting is the real star here, especially the way Miles slowly breaks down his walls. You will love how Gillian uses weird and honest methods to get through to him. While the pace is a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. If you enjoy stories about family secrets and growth, you should definitely check this out. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you want a high-quality copy to keep, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move. It is a touching ride that stays with you long after the credits roll.
endingExplained: By the end, Miles finally admits that his controlling nature pushed Zoe away. He stops trying to fix her and starts fixing himself. In the final scenes, Miles and Zoe have a heart-to-heart conversation where they both apologize and agree to work on their relationship as equals. They leave the facility not as a boss and a subject, but as a father and daughter who truly understand and support each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about family healing and personal growth.
